winRate.short:
Win Rate is the percentage of your closed trades that ended in profit.

Above 55% is solid. But win rate alone doesn't determine success — a trader with 40% WR can be profitable with strong risk-reward ratios. Focus on Profit Factor too.

profitFactor.short:
Profit Factor = Total Gross Wins ÷ Total Gross Losses.

• Above 1.0 = profitable
• Above 1.5 = healthy edge
• Above 2.0 = professional level
• Above 3.0 = exceptional

This is one of the most important metrics in trading.

avgR.short:
Average R-Multiple per closed trade.

R = trade profit ÷ initial risk per share. The profit follows the direction of the trade: on a LONG it is (Exit − Entry), on a SHORT it is (Entry − Exit) — so a winning SHORT is always a positive R.

+1.0R means you made exactly what you risked. Aim for +0.3R or higher as a minimum average. Elite traders average +1.5R to +2.5R.

Only trades that had a stop can be measured in R — a trade without one is excluded from this average, not counted as 0R. The line under the number shows how many of your closed trades the average actually covers.

expectancy.short:
Expectancy = (Win% × Avg Win) − (Loss% × Avg Loss).

Tells you the expected dollar profit per trade on average. Positive = your system has edge. Negative = you're losing money over time regardless of individual wins.

sharpe.short:
Sharpe Ratio measures risk-adjusted return.

• Above 1.0 = good
• Above 2.0 = excellent
• Above 3.0 = exceptional (hedge fund level)

A high Sharpe means consistent returns without wild swings. More important than raw profit for evaluating system quality.

maxDD.short:
Maximum Drawdown — the largest dollar drop from a peak in your account balance to the lowest point before recovery.

A smaller number means fewer large losing streaks and better capital preservation. Deep drawdowns are psychologically damaging and hard to recover from mathematically.

avgHold.short:
Average holding period per closed trade (in days).

Swing trading typically targets 2-10 day holds. Very short holds (< 1 day) often indicate cutting trades too early. Very long holds (> 20 days) may suggest avoiding stop-losses.

equityCurve.short:
Your Equity Curve shows account balance over time.

A smooth, steadily rising curve = consistent edge and good risk management.
Jagged spikes = inconsistent position sizing or emotional trading.
Long flat periods = overtrading without edge.

totalReturn.short: Your total profit or loss since you started, as a percentage of starting capital. The headline performance number — but without risk context it doesn't tell the whole story.

winStreak.short: The number of profitable trades in a row. A winning streak builds confidence — but it's also the most dangerous time for overconfidence and undisciplined risk-taking.

streakHistory.short: A record of your winning and losing streaks over time. It reveals emotional patterns: does a losing streak make you trade worse (tilt), or do you recover with discipline.

grade.short: A weighted score (A–F) summarizing your trading quality for the month: a blend of win rate, R-multiple, discipline and consistency. A quick snapshot — not a substitute for digging into the details.

entryQuality.short: A (star) rating of how well your entry matched the planned setup: timing, price, and confirmation. A consistently high rating signals discipline — even when the trade itself loses.

dayOfWeek.short: Your profit/loss broken down by day of the week. Reveals which days you consistently make or lose money — many traders have a hidden edge (or leak) tied to specific days like Mondays or Fridays.

performanceBySetup.short: A breakdown of every setup you trade — win rate, total R, and number of trades. Shows at a glance which setups carry your account and which drain it. Your edges and anti-edges, side by side.

rr.short: Risk/Reward. Potential profit vs. what you risk. 3:1 = you stand to make 3× what you'd lose.

rMultiple.short:
R-Multiple = trade profit ÷ initial risk. The profit follows the direction of the trade: on a LONG it is (Exit − Entry), on a SHORT it is (Entry − Exit) — so a winning SHORT is always a positive R.

Examples:
+2R = you made 2× what you risked ✓
+1R = made exactly what you risked ✓
-1R = lost your planned risk (normal)
-2R = stop was not honored (problem)

Tracking R-Multiple eliminates dollar bias and lets you compare trades objectively.

mfeMae.short: How far a trade ran in your favor (MFE) and against you (MAE) before it closed. Helps tune stops and targets.

wilson.short: A cautious estimate of your "true" win rate when sample size is small. Stops a short hot streak from fooling you.

rrBucket3plus.short: A group of trades with a risk/reward ratio of 3 or higher — the potential reward is at least 3× the risk. These are the highest-quality trades by ratio: even with a low win rate, winning a fraction of them is enough to be profitable.

dna.short:
Your Trading DNA measures 4 core dimensions of your trading personality:

• Risk Management (0-100): How well you control losses
• Discipline (0-100): Do you follow your rules?
• Consistency (0-100): Stable results across different conditions
• Growth (0-100): Are you improving over time?

Based on your actual trade history — not self-assessment.

edge.short:
Your Edge — setups where you have a statistically significant advantage based on your actual trade history.

High win rate + positive average R = real edge. These are the setups you should trade most. The market is paying you to do these.

antiEdge.short:
Anti-Edge — setups where you consistently lose money based on your trade history.

Low win rate + negative R = your personal anti-edge. Either fix these setups (study why they fail for you) or stop trading them entirely.

Avoiding anti-edges is as important as exploiting edges.

tilt.short:
Tilt — emotional state that causes you to deviate from your trading rules.

Common after: large losses, missing a big move, or a string of wins creating overconfidence.

Signs: increasing position size, trading more frequently, ignoring stops.

Prevention: mandatory break after 2+ consecutive losses.

marketRegime.short:
Market Regime — the current market environment, read from real price action (not your trades). Computed from SPY/QQQ vs their 20-day average, trend %, how many sector ETFs are rising (breadth), and realized volatility.

• Bull Trend: Uptrend — price above a rising 20-day average with broad participation. Favor breakouts and pullbacks.
• Bear Trend: Downtrend — price below a falling 20-day average, broad weakness. Favor shorts or stand aside.
• Choppy/Range: No net trend — price stuck between support and resistance. Fade the extremes, avoid breakouts.
• High Volatility: Large daily swings dominate. Cut size ~50% and widen stops.
• Low Volatility: Quiet, coiled tape — expect small moves.

Shows 'insufficient data' when there isn't enough price history to classify.

discipline.short: Whether you followed your plan — stop, size, target — without emotional deviation. The core of long-term profitability.

dnaRisk.short: Measures how consistent you are at managing risk: uniform position size, respecting stops, and not exceeding your planned per-trade risk. A low score means inconsistent risk — the single biggest threat to an account.

dnaConsistency.short: Measures the stability of your performance over time: are results uniform, or dependent on a few huge trades. High consistency means a method you can rely on; low means random results.

dnaGrowth.short: Measures your improvement trend: are you learning from the data and getting better over time, or repeating the same mistakes. A rising score is the right curve for a developing trader.

riskPerTrade.short:
Maximum risk per trade as % of total account.

Professional standard:
• 1% per trade = conservative, sustainable
• 2% per trade = moderate, still acceptable
• 5%+ per trade = gambling territory

'Risk of ruin' increases exponentially above 2% per trade.

riskLimits.short:
Two limits work together:

• Risk/Trade — the most you risk on a single position. You choose this in Settings.
• Max Allowed Risk — the most you risk across ALL open positions combined. It is derived from Risk/Trade: twice that value, never below 3% and never above 5%.

Divide Max Allowed Risk by Risk/Trade to see how many full-size positions you can hold at once.

positionSize.short:
Position Size = (Account Size × Risk %) ÷ (Entry − Stop Loss)

Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk, $100 entry, $97 stop:
Position = $100 ÷ $3 = 33 shares

Always calculate before entry. Never size by feel.

stopLoss.short:
Stop Loss — the price level where you exit a losing trade to prevent larger losses.

Place at a logical technical level:
• Below key support (long trades)
• Above key resistance (short trades)
• Never arbitrary (e.g., 'just $0.50 below entry')

A stop loss is not optional — it's the foundation of risk management.

takeProfit.short:
Take Profit — your target price for exiting a winning trade.

Minimum rule: Target must be at least 1.5× your risk (1.5R).

Best practice:
• Scale out: take 50% at 1R, hold rest to target
• Use technical levels (resistance, prior highs)
• Never move target lower when winning

breakout.short: Price breaking above a key resistance level with volume. Best in trending markets.

pullback.short: Buying when an uptrending price temporarily retraces toward support — a moving average, a prior breakout level, or a trendline — then resumes higher. Entering on the dip gives a better price and a tighter stop than chasing.

bullFlag.short: Tight consolidation after sharp move up. Volume should contract during the flag.

ORBBreakout.short: Opening Range Breakout — first 15-30 min high/low break. Strong on trend days.

VWAPReclaim.short: Price reclaiming VWAP after morning dip with volume. Indicates institutional buying.

higherLow.short: Each pullback makes a higher low than the previous. Cleanest setup in uptrend.

cupAndHandle.short: U-shaped consolidation with tight handle on right. Classic continuation pattern.

failedBreakout.short: Breakout that quickly reverses. Trap for late buyers — short on reclaim of breakout level.

overextendedFade.short: Counter-trend trade when price is 8%+ above 20 EMA with high RSI. Requires patience.

EMABounce50.short: Pullback to 50 EMA on daily chart. Major support in strong uptrends.

trendContinuation.short: Entry on shallow pullback to 9 EMA in established trend. Tight stops, high R.

gapAndGo.short: Stock gaps up at open and continues higher without filling. Best with news catalyst.

earningsGapPlay.short: Trade the gap reaction post-earnings. Hold winners, cover into first sign of buying.

rangeBreakout.short: Price breaking out of multi-day/week range. Most reliable when volume expands.

postEarningsStrength.short: Stock holds above gap-up after earnings beat. Institutional accumulation signal.

powerHourBreak.short: Breakout in last hour (3-4pm ET). Institutional positioning into close.

MOCFade.short: Market-On-Close fade. Trade against extended moves into close for next-day reversal.

overnightHold.short: Trade held overnight. Higher reward potential but exposed to gap risk.

overnightReversal.short: Trade reversal of overnight move at market open. Counter-trend, requires confirmation.

supportBounce.short: Buying when price drops to a known support level and reverses up. The logic: buyers defend the level. The stop sits below support — if it breaks, the thesis is void.

resistanceBreak.short: Entering when price breaks above a resistance level that previously capped it, ideally on high volume. The break signals buyers have taken control. Differs from a generic Breakout by targeting one specific level.

pullback20EMA.short: Buying when an uptrending price pulls back to the 20-period moving average and bounces. The 20 EMA acts as dynamic support; this setup combines trend with a precise entry point.

emotionConfident.short: Confidence grounded in analysis, not bravado. When based on a valid setup it drives disciplined execution; when it tips into overconfidence after a win streak, it becomes risky.

emotionCalm.short: The optimal emotional state for a trader. Calm lets you follow your plan without chasing or panicking. Trades opened calmly tend to respect their stop and target.

emotionPatient.short: Waiting for a setup that genuinely meets your criteria instead of entering every move. Patience is often what separates a profitable trader from a losing one — it filters out low-quality trades.

emotionNeutral.short: Entering with no emotional charge — neither excited nor fearful. A stable state that allows objective, data-driven decisions. A solid baseline, even if less sharp than "Calm".

emotionHesitant.short: Hesitation at entry — usually a sign the setup isn't clear or confidence is low. Hesitant entries tend to mean entering late, placing the stop too tight, or exiting early out of fear.

emotionNervous.short: Tension that clouds decision-making. Nervousness leads to obsessive price-checking, moving the stop, and impulsive exits. Often a sign the position is too large or the setup isn't trusted.

emotionFOMO.short: "Fear Of Missing Out" — entering a trade just because price moved sharply, with no valid setup. One of the most destructive patterns: late entry, chasing price, and a distant stop. A red flag.

emotionAngry.short: Anger after a loss — the fuel of "revenge trading". In this state a trader tries to win back a loss immediately, raises risk, and takes bad trades. This is how accounts blow up. Stop.

marketTrendingUp.short: An uptrending market: higher highs and higher lows. Long setups work best here; trading against the trend is risky.

marketTrendingDown.short: A downtrending market: lower highs and lower lows. Short setups work best; "catching a falling knife" with a long is dangerous.

marketSideways.short: A market with no clear trend, moving horizontally between support and resistance. Trend setups fail here; range trading (buy support, sell resistance) fits better.

marketVolatile.short: A market with sharp, fast price swings in both directions. Stops get hit easily, and position size should be smaller. Big opportunities but high risk.

chartCalcPosition.short: Auto-fills the Position Calculator from the current chart — ticker, live price as entry, a protective stop and a 2:1 target — then opens it so you can size the trade in one click.

chartAddToJournal.short: Starts a new journal trade from the current chart — ticker, live price, a suggested stop and a 2:1 target pre-filled — ready for you to review and save.
